title: Insta360 X6 Launches With Bigger Sensors, 8K 50fps Video in a Compact Body
excerpt: The next-generation 360-degree action camera pairs dual 1/1.1-inch sensors with a redesigned, shorter body and starts at approximately $800, marking a significant upgrade over the X5.
body:
• Insta360 has launched the X6, its next-generation 360-degree action camera featuring a significantly more compact body and dual 1/1.1-inch sensors that deliver 8K video at up to 50 frames per second.
  • The redesigned camera weighs 195 grams with dimensions of roughly 10 x 5 x 4 cm, making it closer in form to a traditional action camera while retaining full 360-degree capture capabilities.
  • Pricing starts at approximately €689 ($800) for the standard version and €789 ($900) for the Essentials Bundle, representing a notable increase over the X5's €589 launch price.
  • New features include PureVideo low-light mode, Replaceable Lenses 2.0, 10-bit color recording, and a 2,600mAh battery delivering up to 140 minutes of 8K recording.

Insta360 has unveiled the X6, the latest in its flagship 360-degree action camera line, pairing a major design overhaul with meaningful imaging upgrades that position it as the strongest challenge yet to competitors like GoPro and DJI in the immersive video space.

The most immediately visible change is the body. The X6 adopts a shorter, wider form factor that breaks from the elongated shape the X series has carried since the X3. The result looks more like a traditional action camera despite retaining dual fisheye lenses on the front and back for 360-degree capture.

Bigger Sensors, Faster Video

Under the hood, the X6 packs dual 1/1.1-inch CMOS sensors — larger than the 1/1.28-inch units in the X5. Each sensor captures 42 megapixels, enabling 120-megapixel 360-degree photos and 72-megapixel stills in standard mode.

The headline video spec is 8K recording at 50 frames per second in full 360-degree mode, up from the X5's 30fps ceiling. A dedicated PureVideo 360 mode records 8K at 30fps with enhanced low-light processing. In single-lens mode, the camera supports up to 5K at 60fps and 4K at 120fps for slow-motion content.

"The X6 looks more like a GoPro than any of Insta360's previous offerings. This is still classic Insta360, though, with dual camera sensors placed behind a fisheye lens on the front and back sides."

— Gizmodo

Additional imaging features include 10-bit color recording, Dolby Vision support, i-Log color grading for post-production flexibility, and an updated Adaptive Tone 2.0 system for dynamic range optimization.

Compact Design, Larger Battery

At roughly 195 grams and 10 x 5 x 4 cm, the X6 is noticeably more compact than its predecessor while housing a larger 2,600mAh battery. The retail packaging confirms up to 140 minutes of recording at 8K/30fps on a single charge. An Extra Xtreme battery option is included with the Essentials Bundle.

The camera retains a small touchscreen display positioned below the rear lens, with power and record buttons on the side alongside the battery compartment. Microphone openings on multiple sides of the body suggest improved audio capture. A built-in tripod mount on the bottom rounds out the hardware changes.

Insta360 has also introduced Replaceable Lenses 2.0, a second-generation system that allows users to swap out damaged or specialized lenses. The original replaceable lens system on earlier models was a differentiator for adventure creators who frequently risk lens damage.

Pricing and Availability

The X6 starts at €689 (approximately $800) for the standard version, up from the X5's €589 launch price. The Essentials Bundle, which includes the Extra Xtreme battery and additional accessories, is priced at €789 (roughly $900). In India, the expected price is approximately ₹75,999.

The price increase reflects both the component costs of larger sensors and the engineering required to shrink the body without sacrificing performance. Early reviews have been broadly positive, with Forbes calling the X6's improved visuals a sign that it is "no longer just for play" and Gizmodo declaring it "the king of 360 cameras" reclaiming its crown.

What It Means for Creators

The X6 arrives as the 360-degree camera market heats up with competition from DJI's Osmo 360 line. For content creators, travel videographers, and action sports enthusiasts, the combination of larger sensors, faster frame rates, and a more pocketable design addresses the primary complaints about previous-generation 360 cameras: image quality in mixed lighting and the awkward, elongated body that made them difficult to carry and use one-handed.
